payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) begins to melt before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) due to geological and climatic factors during the Last Interglacial (LIG) period, specifically around 125 ka, which is supported by model scenarios that show distinct melting contributions from both ice sheets.

claims.text: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) melts first, contributing to sea level rise at 125 ka, before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) begins to melt at 118 ka.
The early melting of GrIS is linked to continental levering and ocean syphoning, which are significant geological processes during the LIG.
